comment: One row for each gen rule, kill rule and definition of the emptiness pass, the static
overwrite check of D17.11 (src/fort/owner/place.ft, src/fort/owner/prover.ft and
src/fort/owner/report.ft), for its report in a build, under --check and under --fir, and for
the proof that the build-mode pass reads (src/fort/fir_passes.ft). A row names the line that
decides the rule and a text that breaks it. The first stage runs the cases over FIR text and
the examples over fort source (test/fort/owner/prover_test.ft), and the report
(test/fort/owner/report_test.ft). The second runs the build-mode suite
(test/fort/fir_passes_test.ft). The third runs the driver test, which holds the error in
each mode. The fourth holds each program that stopped at run time before the rule became
static against the error at its old site (test/overwrite_oracle_test.py). The table runs in
the Linux VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the product
compiler, whose driver and emitter import owner.prover and owner.report.
The rows D17.11-test hold gen rule 6 of D17.11, the edge of a test against null
(src/fort/owner/place.ft, src/fort/owner/prover.ft, the edge sets of src/fort/fir_flow.ft): the
edge, the kills after the read, the value of the edge, `not`, a named flag, a `switch` whose two
values go to one block, a flag that is memory, the chain of flags, the pointer type of the
place, the bit of a scratch local and the join of an edge set. The prover test holds each over
FIR text (NULLS in test/fort/owner/prover_test.ft).
The rows D17.11-alias hold refinement R6 of spec/ownership-design.md 7, the alias by borrow
and exposure of src/fort/owner/alias.ft that kill rules 3 and 4 of D17.11 read: the exposure of
a call, the result of a call, the copy of storage that a pointer can reach, the exposure of a
store, the operands of an rvalue, the frame of an address, the join, the back edge, the `own`
pointer, the two answers of alias.can_be, the last load of a path and the straight store; and,
proving less, the whole store, the rank of an aggregate result, the limit and the fixpoint
itself. The first stage runs test/fort/owner/alias_test.ft too, which holds each of them.
D17.11-alias-limit-loop, -limit-first, -slice-index, -callee and -address-own came from the
review of R6: the loop that passes the limit on a later turn, the first transfer past it, and
three precision rules; test/fort/owner/alias_test.ft holds each.
